brief: Six decisions that keep a small product simple

slots.subtitle: Six decisions that keep a product understandable, each of them a refusal rather than an addition.
slots.coverNote: The hardest one is on the last page

slots.title: Every option is a decision you handed to the user
slots.subtitle: A setting looks generous and is usually an argument the team could not settle, moved somewhere it will never be resolved.
slots.p1Body: The right one serves most people and makes the setting unnecessary.
slots.p2Body: Every option doubles what has to be tested and explained forever.
slots.p3Body: Adding is easy to justify. Removing is where the discipline lives.
slots.pullQuote: A setting is an argument the team declined to finish.

slots.title: Nothing on the screen is free
slots.subtitle: Each element costs attention whether or not anybody uses it, and the bill is paid by every person who opens the page.
slots.p1Body: If you cannot say what the page is for, neither can anyone else.
slots.p2Body: Frequency should decide prominence, not how hard something was to build.
slots.p3Body: Anything you would not add today is something you can take away.
slots.pullQuote: Attention is the only budget you cannot raise.

slots.title: The shape of the data decides the shape of the product
slots.subtitle: Interfaces can be redrawn in an afternoon. The model underneath them is what everything else has to agree with for years.
slots.p1Body: Two words for the same idea will diverge into two features.
slots.p2Body: Build around what the thing is, not around the screen it appears on.
slots.p3Body: Each boolean added late is a branch every future feature must handle.
slots.pullQuote: Screens are cheap to change. The model underneath is not.

slots.title: Everything you install, you have adopted
slots.subtitle: A library solves this week's problem and joins the list of things that break on somebody else's schedule from now on.
slots.p1Body: If you would not maintain it, you are betting somebody else will.
slots.p2Body: Old and dull has survived the failures the new one has not met yet.
slots.p3Body: Forty lines you understand beats a package you have never opened.
slots.pullQuote: Every install is a promise somebody else gets to break.

slots.title: Pricing is a product decision, not a marketing one
slots.subtitle: It determines who arrives, what they expect and which requests you are obliged to take seriously afterwards.
slots.p1Body: Tiers before you know your customers encode a guess as structure.
slots.p2Body: Free users tell you what is interesting. Paying ones tell you what matters.
slots.p3Body: Increase until you feel resistance. That edge is the actual number.
slots.pullQuote: Price decides who arrives, and what they will ask you for.

slots.title: Simple is a cost you pay continuously
slots.subtitle: It is not a state you reach and keep. Every request is reasonable on its own, and the accumulation of reasonable requests is how products become unusable.
slots.p1Body: A refusal you can point at survives longer than one you remember.
slots.p2Body: Review what was added each quarter and remove one thing deliberately.
slots.p3Body: The complexity you prevented is invisible, which is why it needs a rule.
slots.pullQuote: The complexity you prevented is the work nobody can see.

slots.headline: Take something out
slots.body: Find the option you would not add today, remove it, and see who notices. That is the whole method, and it never stops being the hard part.
slots.signoff: Nobody will thank you for it
